reviews.author: Vee K
reviews.text:
I recently stayed at South Beach State Park Campground, and it’s a great option if you’re looking for a convenient, well-equipped base along the Oregon coast. The campground is massive, with hundreds of sites spread across multiple loops, so it feels more like a small village than a secluded retreat. Despite its size, it’s clean, organized, and fairly quiet overall, with easy access to bathrooms, hot showers, and paved trails. The beach isn’t right next to most campsites, but it’s an easy and scenic walk through dunes and coastal forest, which adds to the experience.

That said, it definitely leans more developed than rustic. Sites can feel a bit close together, especially when it’s busy, so privacy is somewhat limited. If you’re camping near the playground, it can get pretty loud during the day. When I visited at the end of April, the mosquitoes were surprisingly intense, there were a lot of them, especially around dusk, so definitely bring bug spray. On the plus side, the location near Newport is super convenient for food and nearby attractions. Overall, South Beach is a solid, family-friendly campground that prioritizes comfort and location over seclusion, just be prepared for noise and bugs depending on where you’re camped and the time of year.

reviews.author: T Tirey
reviews.text: Cleanest campground we went to on our road trip. The walking trail to the beach was nice, they had a disc golf course, and the showers were free and also clean. Everything was well maintained. The temperature was perfect for cold weather type people like my husband and I. You could hear the crowds of sea lions in the distance, which we thought was funny, though it wasn't disturbingly loud. Slept great with the windows open on the rv. 10/10 would recommend.

reviews.author: Xbox User
reviews.text: Camping and day use picnic area and beach access. Lots of parking available for visitors. I guesstimate about 100+ spots. Paved trail to a nearby jetty (1 mile).

reviews.author: Linfang He
reviews.text: Great campsite. Good privacy and nice amenities. Even better than some private campsites

reviews.author: London L. (snake)
reviews.text: went here with family and we got a spot right next to the playground which wasn't really our plan but it was one of the only spots avaliable. the kids at the playground were active until late at night so it was quite annoying but one night the rangers got them. bathrooms are clean, so are showers, no long lines.

reviews.author: MrsS
reviews.text:
This campground wasn't my first or even 4rth choice. I didn't try to reserve a campsite until the day after it opened for my date, so out of luck. I wanted a site by the ocean, but this campground doesn't offer ANY sites with an ocean view. It's still turned out ok though.

South Beach campground is HUGE! Lots of sites laid out in circles with a bath house in the center. Your best bet is a site on the perimeter. We had C -15, which has to be the best site there! Large & private.

The showers are free. About as clean as any state park usually is, which is fair. Try to avoid a site by the bathroom. Tight sites with no privacy.

We had no issues with noise after quiet hours.

This was one of the few campgrounds on our trip we could have a fire. $5 a bundle, which is the least expensive during out trip.

Newport is one of the larger towns in the area. We did hear traffic noise & the foghorn. Some sirens every day also.

In the campground this is a VERY busy, loud place. If you dislike the sound of children playing, you may hate it here. Lots of skateboards, bikes, scooters & people walking on the roads. Be careful driving & take it slow.

There's beach access you can walk to or drive to. The beach looked nice. Some trails also.

All in all, we had a very good time here. Although we didn't feel unsafe, we didn't leave much of anything out either.

I would recommend making a reservation as early as possible. Every campground we passed in a 70 mile radius had NO vacancy signs.

reviews.author: Cynthia K
reviews.text: Lots of spaces, fairly close together, but with lots of trees. Heated bathrooms!! Also, special family/handicapped bathroom/shower rooms. Great place for winter camping (we were in van). They also have heated yurts at a reasonable rate. Close to beach and hiway, but very quiet.

reviews.author: Kerrie Anne L
reviews.text: What a beautiful beach here! We had a nice camping experience at this park- decent, quiet sites close to beach just watch out for mosquitoes at dusk! Oregon state parks are awesome.

reviews.author: KhmerloveTravels
reviews.text:
Chose this place for our first yurt experience. It did not disappoint! It is the way to go when you have young kids. The yurt was exactly like the pictures I saw online. It even had electricity which was great because I could charge my phone.

The location is perfect. Not too far from Portland, and a short walk to the beach. We did bring our stroller on the walk and while it was good for a while, it got too sandy and we had to ditch the stroller.

The beach was quiet. We had it pretty much to ourselves! Our dog loved it too!

We were able to buy a lighter and firewood when we got there.

reviews.author: mynameisD
reviews.text:
This is a large campground and it was pretty busy for Feb. The spots were average, it was a bit noisy near the playground area.

I enjoyed all the trails you can take to get to the beach. It is the closest campground to Newport that is just a stones throw from the Aquaruim and south jetty and some great birding areas.

It was a fine campground.

reviews.author: Clkinc
reviews.text: This is one of the better state parks on the coast! Well maintained and easily accessible. Nice trails to walk along in many areas. Beautiful scenery and many photo ops! The RV Park and campsite are in an area all their own tucked away which is really nice. It is easy to spend a whole afternoon here just enjoying the beach and the water!

reviews.author: 343cindyr
reviews.text:
This is a huge State Park with something for everyone, but especially the beach. There are no sewer facilities except the one dump station (kind of surprising for a park this large so much have to do with the water table) Campground was full the entire time we were there and is alway popular along 101.

Staff is friendly and we didn't have any problems. Wood and other stuff available at the hospitality hut. The website said that no fires were allowed, but people were having fires, so check with the staff to be sure.

There are hiking/walking trails and beach access throughout the campground and friendly and polite dogs can be off leash at the beach, but not in the campground. Please know your dog as the day we arrived there were several dog bite incidents with not to friendly dogs-what pet owner wants that liability worry!

Nice location close to Newport amenities (shopping, laundry, gas, restaurants) and the Nye Beach area as well as beautiful drive north to Depoe Bay with lots of neat stops on the way.

reviews.author: Sally S
reviews.text: There are NO QUIET HOURS for the I [tent] loop. There are a lot of big groups [same person reserves 2 - 4 total sites]. The people next to us had 4 sites, and of course they chose to all hang out next to us. As we all know, people get louder as they drink, and some were up talking loudly, laughing until 1 am, and then, others were up at 5.45 am. Another site, 2 women were yelling/talking loudly and laughing, non stop until at least 3.30 am.

reviews.author: Apple962421
reviews.text: I was happy to find a spot here for two nights in July of 2025. First Oregon's Coast State Parks are huge! The roads and asphalt are getting tired, sites are close, not much privacy, but it's the coast! Wonderful trails to a big, long and un-inhabited beach. Non-Oregon State residents get to pay more - $55 is high for an average site 20' from the next site. If you have young kids, this would be a great spot! For us, "been there, done that" and would not need to go back.

reviews.author: DFH
reviews.text: Just needed a site for one night. We took a site on a loop away from the close-to-beach sites and were rewarded with few neighbors. Very clean and good working showers. Really close to Newport for loads of good outings. The campground has a number of nature trails as well.

reviews.author: OregonMum
reviews.text: We scored a last minute reservation (only 4 spots open the third week of October) and luckily it had a spot long enough for our truck and trailer.
